findings.title: Escalation placement contradicts its own rule
quotes: the flow places it at the first full-route stage not yet passed
`nio flow next` on the effort says grilling or spec_jury, not tasking or implementing
Given a lite effort past grilling
findings.fix: define "passed" for skipped stages, and make the AC-11 observable name the stage the rule actually gives.

sources.situation: a lite effort at tasking is escalated. Its lite stages skipped researching and advocate_walking, and the spec does not say whether a skipped stage counts as passed. If it does not, the first full-route stage not yet passed is researching, not the grilling or spec_jury that AC-11 promises. If it does, every stage up to tasking counts as passed, so grilling or spec_jury is never reached. Either way the AC-11 observable cannot hold for an effort past grilling.
a lite effort escalates from tasking. Its history has `skip` lines for researching, advocate_walking and spec_jury.

after the switch, one test run gets grilling and another gets spec_jury, and both satisfy the AC. No rule says which stage applies. Nothing says how "not yet passed" is judged for a spec that was rewritten, so a test cannot assert one stage.

findings.reason: AC-11 says the flow places an escalated effort at the "first full-route stage not yet passed", but nothing says whether the lite `skip` lines (AC-1) count as passed. The observable "grilling or spec_jury" cannot follow from either reading for an effort past grilling.
findings.note: a skip never counts as a gate's pass; spec_jury or grilling (grill Q11, delegated)

findings.title: Spec says lite reuses the flow, but the code refuses every non-full route
quotes: existing stages, flow state machine and jury
findings.fix: state that lifting the full-route guard for lite is new work, and add it to the FR list or to a stated change.

sources.situation: src/nio/flow.py lines 334-335 return "unsupported: <route>" for any spec whose route is not full, and line 785 answers "nio flow drives full-route specs only". So nio flow next on a lite effort refuses today. The spec says lite only reuses the existing machinery and never says this route guard changes. AC-1 ("the flow is driven to done") cannot be met by reuse alone.

findings.reason: src/nio/flow.py:335 returns `unsupported: <route>` for any non-full route, and line 785 answers "nio flow drives full-route specs only". The spec calls lite pure reuse (Summary, non-goals), and no FR lifts the guard.
findings.note: FR-15 states the flow drives lite specs

findings.title: Non-goal says no new state machine, yet the lite transition table adds transitions the existing table lacks
quotes: New stages, a new flow state machine or a new jury; lite reuses the existing ones.
### State table: Lite effort (start: intake; final: done, full route)
findings.fix: say the lite table is a route-specific view or override of the existing machine, and list the transitions that differ.

sources.situation: the lite table has "grilling | → tasking" and "implementing | → implementing" on a jury rejection. The existing table in src/nio/flow.py (lines 16-19) sends grilling to spec_jury and implementing to done, with no reject loop. A reader who trusts the non-goal would expect the lite table to be the existing one. The two disagree.

findings.reason: spec-consistency: the non-goal now says the table gains only a per-route set of skipped stages, but the lite table's grilling → tasking and implementing → implementing transitions are not listed as differences from the existing table, and the non-goal does not account for them.
findings.note: FR-2 lists the transitions that differ: grilling → tasking from the skips; implementing's reject loop is the existing implementation gate's

findings.title: Escalation trigger is called objective, but the spec says the triggers are judged
quotes: an objective condition that stops a lite effort and offers the full flow.
needs a new dependency, or changes an interface used outside the bug's folder or stored data
A deterministic check for a new dependency or an interface change; those triggers are judged by the agent from the skill's list.
findings.fix: change "objective" to "stated in the skills", or name which triggers are checked and which are judged.

sources.situation: the key-entity definition says an escalation trigger is objective. FR-8's dependency and interface triggers are judged by the agent, as the non-goal says. A worker who reads "objective" may expect a check that does not exist for these two triggers.

findings.note: key entity: stated in the skills, folder trigger checked

findings.title: A declined switch cannot continue on lite, because the module check keeps failing
quotes: THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL stop the effort and offer the full flow
the check exits non-zero and its message names each folder and says to offer the full flow
THE SYSTEM SHALL continue the effort on lite and log the human's call
findings.fix: define how a logged decline overrides the folder check (for example, the check passes when `grill.md` records the override). Or say the check only warns once the decline is logged.

sources.situation: a lite effort's tasks change non-test files in `src/a` and `src/b`. `nio check tasks` fails (AC-9) and the effort stops (FR-8). The human declines the switch, and FR-11 says the effort continues on lite. The tasks check still sees two folders, so it still fails. The effort cannot pass tasking to tasks_jury unless the check is bypassed, and no override is specified. Either the decline leaves the effort stuck, or the folder trigger is not a hard stop.

findings.reason: AC-9 makes `nio check tasks` fail on more than one folder, and FR-11/AC-12 only log a decline in `grill.md`. Nothing tells the check to honour that log, so a declined effort stays blocked at tasking.
findings.note: folder trigger is a note with an exact folder rule (grill Q10, delegated)

findings.title: "First full-route stage not yet passed" is ambiguous because lite records skips
quotes: then the flow places it at the first full-route stage not yet passed
a `skip` line for each of researching, advocate_walking, spec_jury, arch_grilling, planning and plan_jury
findings.fix: state which stages the full route must re-run after escalation (for example, spec_jury at minimum) and whether a recorded skip counts as passed.

sources.situation: a lite effort escalates from tasking. Its history has `skip` lines for researching, advocate_walking and spec_jury.

findings.title: UJ-2 triggers do not match FR-8
quotes: the fix touches several modules, needs a new dependency or changes a contract
changes an interface used outside the bug's folder or stored data
findings.fix: use one trigger list, and make UJ-2 refer to FR-8.

sources.situation: a fix changes a contract that is used only inside the bug's folder. UJ-2 says to escalate. FR-8 and AC-16 say not to. Stored-data changes have no named equivalent in UJ-2.

findings.title: Risk flags outside the five do not stop lite routing
quotes: no risk flag from auth, money, data-deletion, migration or PII applies
auth | pii | money | external-input | data-deletion | migration | multi-party | public-api
findings.fix: say whether the other three flags are deliberately allowed on lite. If not, add them to FR-12 and the decision table.

sources.situation: a defect with obvious expected behaviour, one module and the flag `external-input` or `public-api` gets route lite. The template defines eight risk flags and FR-12 checks five. For `public-api` a later escalation may catch it, but only if the fix changes an interface used outside the bug's folder. UJ-1's misuse line ("routes a risky ... change as lite") is only partly covered.

findings.note: other three flags stay lite, lenses as usual (grill Q12, delegated)

findings.title: Nested folders and non-code files make the "more than one folder" trigger unclear
quotes: **Module**: a folder holding the changed non-test files, as counted for the escalation trigger.
findings.fix: define the folder count, for example top-level module or nearest common folder, and say whether docs are excluded.

sources.situation: a fix changes `src/a/x.py` and `src/a/sub/y.py`. It is unclear whether that is one folder or two. A fix that also edits `docs/CHANGELOG.md` has non-test files in two folders and so escalates, although it is one module.

a fix touches `src/a/x.py` and `src/a/sub/y.py`. Is that one folder or two? Does a root-level file count as a folder? `conftest.py` or fixtures under `tests/` may or may not be "test files". Two implementations can disagree and both match the AC.

findings.reason: The Glossary defines Module only as "a folder holding the changed non-test files". It is silent on nested folders, docs and root-level files, and on what counts as a test file, so two implementations could disagree.

findings.title: AC-8 asserts a behaviour but its test only reads a card
quotes: Given an unchanged-behaviour test, when it runs on the code before the fix and after it, then it passes on both.
the tasks drafter card says that on a bug fix each unchanged-behaviour test is its own `direct` task
findings.fix: add an integration check on a fixture that runs the unchanged task before and after the fix and expects green both times. Alternatively, reword the AC and FR-7 as "the card instructs" and say the behaviour is judged at the implementation gate.

sources.situation: the drafter card carries the sentence, so the test passes. The drafter still emits a "unchanged" test that fails on the pre-fix code, or one that does not depend on the fix's task. FR-7 is broken and the AC stays green.

findings.reason: AC-8 asserts that the test passes before and after the fix, but its Observable (Level: unit) only checks that the drafter card contains a sentence. FR-7's behaviour is never exercised.
findings.note: FR-7/AC-8 state the card instruction, judged at the tasks jury (grill Q13, delegated)

findings.title: AC-11 cannot name a single expected stage
quotes: `nio flow next` on the effort says grilling or spec_jury, not tasking or implementing
findings.fix: state the deterministic rule, for example "re-enter at grilling when passed stages are drafting and grilling". Then give each case an expected stage.

sources.situation: after the switch, one test run gets grilling and another gets spec_jury, and both satisfy the AC. No rule says which stage applies. Nothing says how "not yet passed" is judged for a spec that was rewritten, so a test cannot assert one stage.

findings.title: NFR-2 has no baseline, no definition of "small" and no pass rule
quotes: complete a small lite effort at least 15 minutes faster in wall-clock than the same effort on the full flow
findings.fix: define a reference effort (a named bug with a size cap), the number of runs and the pass rule. Or downgrade NFR-2 to a reported measure that is not pass/fail.

sources.situation: "the same effort on the full flow" has to be run twice, and each run varies by minutes. SC-1 only says the time is "reported". Nothing says what happens if the gap is 14 minutes. "Small" has no size limit, so no test can fail the NFR.

findings.reason: NFR-2 sets a 15-minute margin against "the same effort on the full flow" without defining "small", the number of runs or a pass rule. SC-1 only says the time is "reported".
findings.note: NFR-2 is a reported measure (grill Q13, delegated)

findings.title: AC-2 states a count of questions but its test checks only a text sentence, and "the bar" is undefined
quotes: then it asks the human zero questions
the grill skill says that on a lite spec it skips the six-facet coverage and asks only points over the bar
findings.fix: define the bar as "open point of kind decision" in the AC. Test it against a fixture spec with no open decision and one with an open decision.

sources.situation: the Observable never mentions zero questions and never says what the bar is. A grill that asks one question about a non-decision point still passes the text test. FR-12's "obvious" and "likely" criteria have the same problem, so a test cannot tell which intake is lite.

findings.note: AC-2 names the bar and the zero-question case

findings.title: Needs-a-decision escalation trigger dropped while Decisions says it was kept
quotes: The "needs a decision" trigger folds into the grill's bar and FR-8's list
needs a new dependency, or changes an interface used outside the bug's folder or stored data
findings.fix: add "the expected behaviour needs a human decision with two or more real options" to FR-8 and to AC-16, or delete the Decisions sentence and record on purpose that the trigger was dropped.

sources.situation: #44 (intake) lists "the expected behaviour needs a human decision with two or more real options" as an escalation trigger. A lite bugfix whose expected behaviour has two real options reaches the grill, FR-3 has the human answer, and no requirement stops the effort or offers the full flow. FR-8 and AC-16 name only the new dependency, interface and stored-data triggers, so the effort stays on lite with the trigger gone, even though Decisions says it was kept.

findings.reason: The Decisions line says the "needs a decision" trigger "folds into the grill's bar" and that FR-9 was retired in grill Q5. That is a recorded choice: the grill (FR-3, AC-2) handles real decisions, not an escalation. The finding's claim that Decisions "says it was kept" misreads "folds into".

findings.title: Tasks stage kept on lite, reversing the skip list the human approved in #44
quotes: tasks and their jury, then implementing
Lite runs intake, drafting, grilling, tasks and the tasks jury, then implementing with the implementation jury
findings.fix: have the human confirm the reversal of #44's tasks skip and record it as [human], or drop tasks from the lite stage list and have implementing read the bugfix spec.

sources.situation: the intake quotes #44 as "Skipped: research fan-out, Actors and journeys, user advocate walk, architecture grill, plan and tasks stages." The spec runs tasks and the tasks jury on every lite effort and tags the reversal as [agent] (grill Q1). If the human did not confirm this reversal in the grill, the lite route adds a jury and a stage that the human's own issue removed, which works against the 15-minute target in NFR-2. The rationale is sound (implementing reads tasks.md), but it needs the human's confirmation or a tag change.

findings.reason: spec-scope: FR-2 now states the departure from #44's tasks skip, but the grill Q1 it cites is still tagged [agent] in Decisions. The fix asked for the human to confirm it or for the item to be tagged [human]. Neither was done.
findings.note: Delegated: the human gave the orchestrator standing authority to take the recommended option; keeping the tasks stage (Q1) and the gate's usual lenses (Q2) are recorded in the decision matrix for the human to review on the PR.

findings.title: Implementation gate keeps the usual lenses, not the one-lens default in #44
quotes: review the fix diff with its usual lenses
The implementation gate keeps its usual lenses on a lite fix
findings.fix: state the lens set in FR-13 (for example the one correctness lens plus risk-triggered lenses) and cite the human's answer, or record the usual set as a human decision with its cost.

sources.situation: the intake quotes #44's default as "the `low` ladder rung with one core lens: `correctness`" plus triggered lenses. The spec gives every lite fix the usual lens set, which is more than the default the human's issue chose. For a one-module typo fix this adds review cost against the 15-minute target. Nothing in the intake asks for the heavier set.

findings.reason: spec-scope: FR-13 now states the lens set and the departure from #44's default, which is the concrete part asked for. The cited answer (grill Q2) is still [agent], so the human's answer is not cited, and the cost of the heavier set is not recorded.
findings.note: Delegated: the human gave the orchestrator standing authority to take the recommended option; keeping the tasks stage (Q1) and the gate's usual lenses (Q2) are recorded in the decision matrix for the human to review on the PR.
